- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive lag.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with momentum.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is evident when forecast deviates >5% from 14-day moving average; apply correction toward that average.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in second half of horizon.
